answer_1.quote: We evaluate Jawaher using both open-and closed-source state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs (mLLMs) to assess their abilities across our proposed tasks... We create a universal prompt template in English... to produce the output.
answer_1.outputs: The models generate translations and explanations of Arabic proverbs in both English and Arabic.

answer_2.quote: We use BLEURT and BERTScore to judge the quality of explanations and translations.

answer_3.quote: Recently, LLMbased evaluation has emerged as a scalable and cost-effective alternative to human evaluations. In this work, we use LangChain's 4 evaluation framework with string evaluator. We specifically customize the evaluation criteria to our own and use GPT-4o for evaluation.
methods: LangChain's evaluation framework with string evaluator

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluation to assess model performance. We develop evaluation criteria tailored to the nature of our tasks. Human evaluation is carried out by two expert annotators, both holding degrees in linguistics and translation studies...
answer_4.guideline: We assess the models based on accuracy and idiomaticity for translation, and for explanation tasks, we evaluate clarity, depth & detail, correctness, and cultural relevance and sensitivity.
